_note: The DSX Scene FRAME corpus (dsx-scene.md P4): the on:frame contract AS DATA. THE LAW: `on:frame` is a scene-root handler that receives a tick payload { dt, elapsed, frame } — dt = SECONDS since the previously EMITTED tick (0 for the first), elapsed = seconds since the first tick, frame = the emitted-tick counter starting at 0; all three are non-negative, elapsed and frame are strictly monotonic. THE BUDGET LAW: at most 60 ticks per second — a raw platform tick arriving less than 1000/60 ms after the last EMITTED tick is COALESCED (dropped; its time folds into the next emitted dt), so a 120 Hz display emits every second-or-later frame and a store-driven static scene pays nothing. THE LIFECYCLE LAW (stated here, asserted by each surface's own tests — a data corpus cannot mount elements): the tick loop runs ONLY while an on:frame handler is authored AND the element is connected/mounted; it stops when the element unmounts; a scene without on:frame runs NO loop at all (the P1 no-free-running-loop law stands for static scenes). Handlers run through the SAME runner path as on:tap, with dt/elapsed/frame as the payload. Case shape: `ticks` = raw platform tick timestamps in MILLISECONDS (what requestAnimationFrame / withFrameNanos / CADisplayLink hand the surface); `expect` = the emitted payload list, seconds to 6 decimals, tolerance 1.5e-6 — computed by an independent scratch implementation. Runners: TS (per-PR), Kotlin (:core). Swift is the NAMED P4 follow-up (dsx-scene.md P4 row).
